requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied tests answer each question.

The subject's obligations map to the tests as follows.

- **Ordinary comments excluded.**
  - `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments]` puts a plain `// {cite}` line comment between the attribute and the function. It changes that comment's text between variants and asserts the hash is unchanged.
  - `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a Rust case with a `/* note */` block comment inside the function body. Editing it must leave the fingerprint equal.
- **Doc comments participate.**
  - Changing `Doc.` to `Docs.` changes the hash in the first test above.
  - `fn[editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash]` asserts that changing a word and dropping the final `.` both change the hash.
  - `fn[reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` asserts that reordering or changing a word changes the hash.
- **Delimiters excluded and reflow preserves the hash.**
  - `fn[reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` shows `/// a` + `/// b`, `/// a b`, padded and blank-separated `///` lines, and a `/** … * b */` block all hash the same.
  - `fn[reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` covers inner `//!` and `/*! */` forms on a module. It also shows `/** * */` equals `///`.
  - Together these cover the `///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/` and leading `*` delimiters.
- **Consecutive comments of one group hash as one word sequence.** Covered by the reflow tests above and by `fn[inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups]`, which splits words across consecutive `//!` lines. The reflow tests also show that reordering words changes the hash.
- **Inner and outer groups are distinct.** `fn[inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups]` asserts that moving a word from a nested item's `///` into the module's `//!` changes the module hash.
- **Whitespace-separated words, with `ab cd` differing from `abcd`.** `fn[prose_words_are_encoded_separately]` asserts `/// ab cd` differs from `/// abcd`. `fn[string_literals_hash_as_words]` and the Rust case in `fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` cover literals and doc prose, including that extra whitespace does not matter.
- **Attributes attached to an item participate.** `fn[hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments]` asserts that changing `#[inline]` to `#[cold]` changes the hash. `fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]` asserts that the selected span includes the attribute and doc comment, that a formatted variant matches, and that changing the body changes the fingerprint.
- **SHA-256 form.** The bundled-fingerprints test asserts a 64-character hex digest. No test pins a known SHA-256 value. The encoding is unspecified, so a known value could not be derived from the text. The length and hex checks plus the equality and inequality assertions are reasonable evidence here.
- **Fingerprint scheme.** `fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts the Rust scheme is `rust-structural-v1`. It also asserts that loaded content retains it. The scheme requirement is cited, so I did not reassess it.

I found no obligation, boundary or failure case that lacks a test with an assertion, and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
